yan: One yang below, veiled by a host of yin, is like leaving what one relies upon and meeting a fierce enemy. This hexagram greatly favors keeping to the old and does not favor making changes. The far traveler has not returned. The sick grow worse. It is the image of parting and separation.
he: In office there is no advancement; in livelihood there is no profit. One’s dwelling is lonely and mean; in poverty and want one clings to one’s lot. The imprisoned find it hard to come out. The sick do not recover. All that one does fails to please the heart, and marriage has no beginning or end.
chen: The human way is weak while the earthly way is strong; four lines enclose from above, the ground of harmony is lacking, and the yang finds nothing to answer it.
liu: “Thin quilt, single garment” means lowly and alone. Yin flourishes and hides above, with none to join in vigor. In this hexagram one yang lies beneath abundant yin and finds no response, like an orphaned child. Four, with its crooked yin, dwells above, like a jealous woman glaring at an orphan — its distress is extreme. Divining about illness means danger and distress. The traveler is detained and in trouble. In office one meets with misfortune. One’s livelihood does not prosper. Marching with troops is hard. In all affairs there is misfortune.
shi: The warm yang lacks the power to nurture; cold and bare, no spring takes shape. Like a dream of Mount Wu — all in vain, it vexes and grieves the man.

name: Hexagram of the Hidden Dragon
note: One yang restraining yin; Kan, water of the due north.
xiang: Shun tilled the fields himself, going to Mount Li; the soil was rich, the year abundant, and the harvest reached ten thousand.
yan: All affairs begin in the third or fourth month and are completed in the eighth or ninth — auspicious. It is also said: to dwell in concealment and till the fields oneself in answer to a year of plenty — who could do this but Shun? This hexagram is the same as the first line of Qian: keeping the person safe and dwelling in concealment, one may cultivate within oneself the virtue of a sovereign. In affairs, great or small, if one entrusts them to the Way all is well; but it is hard to scheme and seek. The sick will not recover until the end of autumn.
he: Farming and sericulture are fitting; what is sought is gained. Trade brings profit. Staying at home brings wealth. The traveler soon returns. A pregnant woman bears a son. Marriage is harmonious. All affairs are auspicious.
chen: One occupies the human position and two the earthly position, yin and yang in mutual accord; four yin are in Heaven, giving the image of cloud and rain; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Accumulated yin above” means exhaustion, with none to join it. “Virtue abundant and answered” means dwelling in the low place. “When the hour comes, it rises” means nothing can withstand it. In this hexagram, though one yang stands amid a host of yin, the upper yin is abundant to the extreme and its way is already spent. The lesser yin below is my neighbor. Though above does not look back, below responds; hence the image of Shun tilling Mount Li. Though unloved by his parents, his primal virtue in the end rose to be heard.
shi: The luck has come, the season prospers; the anxious heart is freed of sorrow. Fully fit for advance and use, in every affair one may roam at ease.

name: Hexagram of the Helpful Friend
note: Yang below transforming yin; Dui, lake of the due west.
xiang: A guest, a scion of kings, comes and knocks at my gate; he tells me of blessing and joy — going, I shall receive his grace.
yan: Only when someone calls should one go; if there is a call and one does not go, that is not auspicious — the text says it is fitting to go. If the traveler is abroad, call him and he will return. It is also said: with the inner responding to the outer, one does not rest within but sets one’s will on going, because the central position gives help. A guest so noble — who could it be but a scion of kings? In this hexagram marriage is timely, and seeking grows all the more excellent.
he: Farming and sericulture yield harvest. The sick recover. Official affairs dissolve. The traveler arrives. Seeking office and meeting the eminent, one will surely gain an introduction. All affairs follow the heart — greatly auspicious.
chen: Three occupies the earthly position — the image of a worthy man below; it responds to the four yin above, and one yang is of its own kind, so that one may be introduced and rise together.
liu: “A scion of kings knocks at my gate” means the response is without. “Going, I receive grace” means there is help. In this hexagram exhausted yin is above and abundant yang below; yin at its extreme has the will to seek yang, and so it is the image of coming to knock at my gate. The scion of kings is a man noble and flourishing. The central position is lesser yang, which does not contend with me but helps me, and so going is sure to bring celebration. In divination, affairs favor advancing, and there will surely be the help of a noble man. The sick will meet with a good physician. In using troops, there will be someone who comes to answer. In everything there is good fortune.
shi: The hour has come; your plans must succeed; Heaven’s grace is about to arrive, and a letter comes in glory. The lifelong aim that never before was fulfilled — today, meeting you, at last it gratifies the heart.

name: Hexagram of Growing Villainy
note: A host of yin restraining yang; Kan, water of the due north.
xiang: Parted and dwelling apart, again and again, many hindrances; in all affairs it is unfavorable, and nothing undertaken can be raised up.
yan: One yang at the center cannot cross over alone. The host of yin cling together and bring harm again and again. The affairs one undertakes mostly fail to follow the heart, and instead there is fright and dread, because the one yang cannot cross over alone. Though one withdraws and hides in secrecy, it is hard to preserve oneself whole; for the time being one must keep to the old and cannot easily make plans or decisions.
he: Travelers by water and land are overturned and ruined. The sick do not recover. The imprisoned do not come out. Those in office should ask for leave. This hexagram is greatly inauspicious.
chen: One yang, solitary and weak, stands between the hosts of yin above and below, with nothing to answer it. It has the image of the pitfall of Kan. The way of petty men grows, villainy and crookedness rise together, and home and state are not at peace; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Parted and dwelling apart” means distress, with none to join it. Solitary and slender, how can it raise anything up? In this hexagram the solitary yang is sunk amid accumulated yin and cannot bestir itself; in all affairs there is misfortune.
shi: Detained through the years, he has not yet come home; when the affair was about to succeed, the mind turned aside. Growing old in poverty and sorrow, for his lot is harsh — I counsel you: do not resent the world’s coldness.

name: Hexagram of Warning Against Advance
note: A host of yin in reversed places; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: In drunkenness a fight breaks out; knives and staves are raised at once; the host is terrified, and only binds himself to make it stop.
yan: Dwelling in a place without position, beneath a host of yin, host and guest forget the rites; drunken and angry, they clamor and contend, and the host humbles himself, and only then does it stop. This hexagram has much blame, and entertaining guests is inauspicious.
he: At first there are disputes; resolve them gently, and in the end there is no worry. At home guard against matters of women and bloodshed; official affairs, goods and money, and illness are all unfavorable, but performing rites of averting evil brings good fortune. The traveler should fear quarrels. In all affairs one should be cautious and vigilant.
chen: Both positions are yin; the host cannot prevail over the guest, and so there is harm from robbers, from which one withdraws; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Drunken clamor and contention” is the misfortune of petty men. “The host binds himself” means he avoids their edge. Youming says: dwelling in a place without position, beneath a host of yin and with no aid or support, host and guest forget the rites; drunken and angry, they clamor and contend, and the host humbles himself, and only then does it stop — an image of much blame. Chengtian says: at first there are disputes; resolve them gently and there will be no worry. In this hexagram it is not fitting to conduct affairs; one can only preserve oneself.
shi: In handling affairs, you must think them through; in seeking and planning, watch for the right moment. Before the wine-cup, beware the violent guest — with humility and retreat you may avoid all harm.

name: Hexagram of Divine Aid
image: Image of Adversity at Its Utmost
note: One yang surviving alone; Zhen, thunder of the due east.
xiang: Four masters and two talismans, face to face, heads uplifted; the heavenly spirits descend, releasing the bound prisoners; disaster and harm are removed and healed — truly one gains Heaven’s protection.
yan: All affairs are released and resolved. Doubled yin is in Heaven, and the ghostly breath shifts; one yang alone survives. To remove trouble and dispel disaster — who but the heavenly spirits could answer this? In all affairs, misfortune comes first and good fortune after.
he: Undertaking affairs jointly with others is auspicious. Marriage is harmonious. The imprisoned are released. The sick recover. The traveler arrives at once. A pregnant woman bears a son. Silkworms and grain give a meager harvest. Grievances and enmities are cleared away of themselves.
chen: Four yin above, with ghosts and spirits mingled among them. The middle and lower respond to each other and cover one another. One yang occupies the earthly position, holding the root of goodness; as its lord, the will to life is not cut off. The heavenly spirits send down blessings upon it; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Four masters, two shamans” means yin flourishes and ascends. “The heavenly spirits send down blessing” means at the extreme of distress comes success. In this hexagram yin flourishes above, the image of ghosts and spirits. Lesser yin at the center, of its own kind and concealed, is the image of the shaman. Though the one yang is faint and cannot bestir itself, when the young man and young woman seek, they are sure to join; hence they pray on my behalf above, and blessings descend and calamities are removed — so that what flourishes above is no ghost but the heavenly spirits. It is the image of the utmost turning to peace. In divination, entrusting affairs to others, one gains strength; there is distress first and joy after.
shi: Heaven’s rain falls like a long, soaking shower; vast and boundless, the virtue and moisture are new. The withered root revives, the stagnant breaks free — in a single day the ford is open.

name: Hexagram of Release Through Sacrifice
note: Accumulated yin without yang; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: The family tomb upon the high mound, where ghosts and spirits roam above; it is fitting to make appeasing offerings there, and one may be free of worry.
yan: Accumulated yin without yang, its height lofty and towering — the image of a family tomb. The way of ghosts and spirits is flourishing; only by sincere sacrifice and offering can one be free of worry.
he: If one has promised something to another and not given it, giving it brings good fortune. If strange things are seen, it is fitting to sacrifice to the spirits of the mounds and hills — auspicious. In illness, an ancient tomb with a hidden corpse is doing harm, and it should be resolved. A birth produces a daughter. The traveler abroad has the help of someone of the yin sort and will return of his own accord by summer. This hexagram is mediocre.
chen: Accumulated yin above, with the middle and lower all yin — the image of a ghostly vapor filling all. The yang force is already cut off, and the human way has no rescue. Hasten to pray with a sincere heart; hence the text says as above.
liu: “The tomb upon the high mound” means the ghostly vapor flourishes; hasten to release it with offerings, obediently receiving one’s fate. In this hexagram four yin occupy the upper, and the middle and lower are all lesser yin with no yang, and so it is the image of a lofty family tomb. Only by reverence, obedience, and dutiful service can one escape disaster. The diviner should not strive and contend; in all affairs, to deal with them with gentleness, obedience, and uprightness is auspicious.
shi: Do not debate failure and success; worry rather amid your illness. Only repay with hidden virtue, and the Creator’s deep work will answer.

name: Hexagram of Checking Disaster’s Force
note: Yang below restraining yin; Zhen, thunder of the due east.
xiang: The metal spirit is about to rise; relying on a great man, with the left hand he presses it down, and so it is quelled and set right.
yan: Metal is the position of the lesser yin of the west, governing weapons, war, and killing. The great man is a person of eminence. The left is yang. This says: the yin vapor is about to stir and do harm, but a great man comes to help, presses it down with the left hand, and the harm is extinguished — yang is able to govern yin. In this hexagram there is anxiety, but it does not become utter disorder.
he: In this hexagram, whether going out or staying, in plans and hopes, anxiety comes first and joy after; in all affairs, one must gain the help of a great man for good fortune. Whether going out or staying, in plans and hopes, all affairs come to completion through the help of a gentleman, and disaster turns into blessing. Official affairs are auspicious; hoping on a powerful official, one is spared. One must also be vigilant and cautious, and in all affairs keep to the ordinary.
chen: Four above and two in the middle, the yin vapor descends from Heaven — the image of weapons about to rise. Three yang below can give the multitude peace, and responding to four, it gains the blessing of the world; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Lesser yin ascends” means the metal spirit rises. “Three yang govern it” means they obtain its ceasing. In this hexagram exhausted yin dwells above and lesser yin is in the middle; two is the image of Dui, and so it is called the metal spirit. Three yang below answer the upper, and the lesser yin cannot put its power to use. The left is yang; in all affairs, gaining the help of a great man, one is cautious first and joyful after.
shi: For years the leopard hides in the deep mist, awaiting change; one day the roc spreads its wings and soars straight up to Heaven. If you gain the strength of a man whose word is gold, honor and nobility will surely come within the year.

name: Hexagram of Prayer for Success
note: Yin at its extreme above and below; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: With sacrifice at the ancestral temple, disaster and harm cease and stop; blessing comes to the door, and calamity departs ten thousand li.
yan: A host of yin above is the image of the ancestral temple. Official affairs dissolve. The sick recover. Dreams are topsy-turvy. In all affairs it is fitting to sacrifice at the temple and seek blessings; making offerings to the spirits is auspicious.
he: On seeing strange things and in all affairs, sacrifice at the temple and seek blessings, and there will be good fortune. A birth produces a daughter. Guard carefully against fire and candle.
chen: The ghosts of Heaven and humanity gather together, and the human way is weak in yin — the image of a ghostly vapor bringing illness. Though one sacrifices and seeks release, afterward there will still be disaster.
liu: “Sacrifice at the ancestral temple” means the place where the spirits repose. Receive them with reverence, and there will be blessing and no calamity. In this hexagram above and below are both four yin: the upper is the ancestral temple and the lower is the tomb mound, while two, as lesser yin, occupies the central position — like a person serving gods and ghosts, reverent, obedient, and dutiful; if one does not lose the rites, one receives blessing without calamity. For the diviner, it is auspicious.
shi: A table lacking one leg is hard to steady; a tripod with two feet is hard to stand. All that you hope and seek in the end costs labor — earnestly pray for blessing, and escape injury and harm.

name: Hexagram of Warning Against Encounter
image: Image of Knowing When to Stop
note: Yang dwelling in yin’s place; Zhen, thunder of the due east.
xiang: Before you are robbers and thieves, behind you no one travels the road; walk calmly and stay your going, and you may keep your body whole.
yan: Three yang dwell together, with no position below; a host of yin above is like robbers in front. Yet the three yang are just beginning to flourish; walking calmly and staying the journey, they cannot be harmed. Though there is no great joy, one can barely keep the body whole. This hexagram is mildly auspicious for travel. It is also said: below, four has no position, and so it is said that behind there is no traveler.
he: At first there are disputes; if you wish to return to your native place, it is fitting for now to pause, and then you may escape trouble. All affairs carry small blame. This hexagram does not favor going; it favors stopping, and in all affairs one should be slow.
chen: Crooked yin above, with the host firm and strong, is enough to govern it; hence the text says as above.
liu: “A host of yin above” means robbers before. “Having the upper without the lower” means no one behind. Knowing the difficulty and stopping, one may be without blame.
shi: To set out now is not easy — many obstructions; and beware the petty men of yin who wound in the dark. A stick of fine incense, offered in thanks and averting — pray for protection, dispel disaster, and your body will be well.

name: Hexagram of Following the Heart
note: The yang host honoring yin; Dui, lake of the due west.
xiang: Primal clouds are above, below there is no slanderer; all affairs flow freely, and all return to the true.
yan: All affairs follow the heart, and one gains the help of others. It is also said: yin occupies the upper position, honored by the host of yang; disaster departs and blessing comes, and affairs proceed from sacrifice. In this hexagram, sacrifice at the ancestral temple is greatly auspicious; the household is peaceful and serene, and forever keeps free of blame.
he: A pregnant woman bears a son. The traveler arrives at once. Disputes bring no suffering. For illness, it is fitting to sacrifice and seek blessings, and then one will recover. Farming and sericulture yield harvest. Greatly auspicious and favorable; autumn is fitting for setting affairs in motion.
chen: A host of yin above, while the human way is strong and flourishing; yin and yang communicate with each other, and there is one yang on earth besides, so that wherever one dwells all is at peace.
liu: “Primal clouds above” means yin ascends; “no slanderer below” means the way of yang prospers. In this hexagram four yin are above and the two lower positions are both yang, hence the image of primal clouds. Three, the middle, and the lower each occupy their proper places; the yang is firm with no yin, and there is no slanderer — this is the image of all affairs flowing freely. For the diviner, all affairs are auspicious, and the traveler soon arrives.
shi: Fame and profit are ordinary things, but not so easy to scheme for. When the hour comes and the luck is good, there is no need to spend your effort.

name: Hexagram of Gain and Loss
note: Yin violent, yang surviving; Kan, water of the due north.
xiang: I lost my precious pearl, it was on the highway of Heaven; unlooked-for thieves hid it in their dwelling; but relying on the dark bird, which drove them off for me, the wind stilled, the waves subsided, and I returned to my home again.
yan: In all affairs, one is at first repressed, but afterward all follows the heart; obtaining things through other people does not last long — in all affairs it is so. It is also said: though yin is above, yang has its position; the leader of the yin robbers runs rampant and steals my rare treasure, but relying on the surviving yang, in the end the villainy is cut down. Like that dark bird driving off the evil fowl, when wind and wave are stilled, one may return to the old home. This hexagram is a sign of misfortune first and good fortune after.
he: First repressed, then opened — in all affairs it is so. Farming and sericulture bring profit. A pregnant woman bears a son.
chen: Above and below are both yin, inclined to prevail over yang; yet the human position is strong and flourishing, and they cannot harm it; moreover, upper and middle respond to each other, so what is lost may be regained, enough to govern the strong and the reckless; hence the text says as above.
liu: “I lost my precious pearl” means yin above is exhausted. In this hexagram four yang are exhausted above and two yin grow below, and so it is the image of losing one’s precious pearl, with thieves hiding it in their dwelling. Yet three yang in the middle stands neighbor to the upper, and the lesser yin is soft and weak and cannot withstand it, and in the end cannot do harm. For the diviner, there is obstruction first and peace after, gaining good fortune through the help of others.
shi: Smoothing the brow and opening the eyes, gold comes to light; with a lifting of the will, the rivers and hills reveal the old home. Fishing in the water, the fish is not yet caught — but at the end of the line, suddenly a bright pearl appears.

name: Hexagram of Rescue
image: Image of Returning to the Beginning
note: Yin at its extreme, yang firm; Dui, lake of the due west.
xiang: The Arbiter of Fate descends to examine the records and charts; finding the allotted span not yet spent, though wrongfully and guiltlessly stricken, he at once commands Bian Que to open the jade flask and bestow a pill of medicine, and so one is revived to life.
yan: The sick should take pill medicine; what is sought is gained; the traveler returns.
he: The Arbiter of Fate is the heavenly physician. Though a host of yang is veiled by doubled yin, one is like the guiltless drowned in a wanton calamity; Heaven commands Bian Que to rescue him, and the calamity is removed. This hexagram turns disaster into blessing. The gravely ill do not die. In official affairs, there will first be a flurry of documents, and then the matter is set right and also subsides of itself. This hexagram is misfortune first and good fortune after.
chen: The middle and lower positions are yang exceeding in abundance, and excess becomes disaster. Four yin above can give aid and response to three, tempering the firm with the soft, so that the yang does not reach excess.
liu: “Yang veiled by yin” means great innocence. “Doubled firmness ascending” means in the end it cannot be defiled. In this hexagram the middle and lower are pure yang, and four yin is above, hence the image of the innocent being trapped. Yet the yang is now flourishing; though oppressed for a time, in the end it will not sink — and moreover, yin at its extreme must decline, while the way of yin is now at its height. One will gain the help of the heavenly spirits. In divination, affairs are distressed first and successful after; through disaster one gains blessing. The sick are weary but do not die. Using troops is perilous but ends in victory. In all affairs there is anxiety first and joy after.
shi: That joy comes from Heaven is plain to know; merit and fame have their appointed time. The grieving man’s brow unknits, the drunk comes sober — in one day light is born, shining ten thousand li.

name: Hexagram of Great Harmony
note: Three yang breaking through yin; Kan, water of the due north.
xiang: The highway of Heaven lies open and level, five ways reach out, six roads pass through; I travel along its midst, riding the clouds, driving the dragon.
yan: Three yang at the center, the position honored and in full abundance — I am the yang, the highway of Heaven is open, cloud and dragon follow, and mounting and driving them I command the six directions, like the fifth line of Qian. Whatever obstructs and meets this cannot prevail and returns in utter misfortune. Aiding an enlightened age, one also remains free of blame. Whatever is sought may be followed to its uttermost. Official affairs dissolve. The sick recover. The traveler soon arrives. Trade brings great gain. Marriage is harmonious. This hexagram is a sign of great good fortune.
he: The sun rises in the east and shines upon my northern corner; its lingering light spreads to the dark valleys. Another version says: when the yellow bell is set at the zi pitch, the yang force begins to grow; gradually it reaches peace and harmony, and the six directions sing with joy; all affairs follow the heart, and all that is done is auspicious.
chen: Three yang in the middle, the human way at its fullest; the four yin above and below all respond to it. Heaven gives to it and humanity gives to it — this is called Great Harmony.
liu: “The highway of Heaven lies open and level” means the soft cannot prevail over the firm. “Riding the clouds, driving the dragon” means the position is upright and central. In this hexagram the mature yin above and below can do nothing, while the three yang at the center are firm, bright, and grand, going everywhere without obstruction; hence the image of the open highway of Heaven with five ways and six roads passing through. The diviner who obtains it can set states right, give peace to the common people, and remove the cruel and the violent — nothing is beyond him.
shi: The clouds part and the moon hangs in the sky; at the hour between the Ox and the Rat you meet your chance. Draw the bow till it touches the target, and one arrow settles the work at hand.

name: Hexagram of the Binding Strangle
note: A host of yin growing ever stronger; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: Suspended and urgent, as if being strangled, and no rescue can arrive. Even Lu’s Wang and the Lord Gao are not enough to set beside this.
yan: The virtue of yang is wholly spent, and a host of yin grows ever stronger — the image of ruin and disorder. As when Duke Min of Lu was killed by the villain Ji You, and Duke Xi fled to Zhu, in the winter of that year Lord Gao of Qi came to make a covenant and thereby pacified the troubles of Lu. In this hexagram, a military expedition is defeated first and rejoiced after.
he: Disputes and gossip are tangled and confining. The sick recover slowly. The traveler has not arrived. The army does not prevail. In the household, be careful and guard against servants. In official affairs, anxiety comes first, and afterward one gains the help of others. In seeking office, one should act quickly and it will succeed; otherwise there will surely be ghosts and villains. In this hexagram, in all affairs one should hasten to the rescue and not be slow.
chen: A host of yin above and below, with disaster and upheaval pressing and urgent; one should hasten to rescue it; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Suspended and urgent, as if being strangled” means the extreme of exhaustion. “No rescue can arrive” means the disaster is imminent. Without a lower position, it is the image of hanging high. In this hexagram a host of yin ascends, and must come to ruin and disorder, while one looks to others for rescue — the depth of distress. For the diviner, all is inauspicious.
shi: Yang at its extreme, the peril is grave indeed; the people already hang upside down. Without the strength of rescue and relief, how can one keep life whole?

name: Hexagram of Sunken Gloom
note: A host of yin veiling yang; Zhen, thunder of the due east.
xiang: Gasping, a thread of breath, with no strength at all; face upward, he cries to Heaven; head bowed, he prostrates on the ground. What he seeks does not get through, what he would see he cannot attain.
yan: Only one yang remains, sunk beneath the earth, veiled by a host of yin; bowing low and prostrate, how much of life is left? This hexagram is greatly inauspicious. The sick are brought to distress. Sericulture disappoints one’s hopes. Trade and seeking bring no profit. Going far away, one meets robbers.
he: In all affairs, one does not know how things stand and can only sigh. In office and in private life, disputes and gossip have already run deep; one should only guard oneself carefully, keep idle and withdrawn, and perhaps go a thousand li away to escape. Official affairs are hard to resolve. The sick are hard to cure. What one does is unfavorable.
chen: The upper and middle positions are yin exceeding in abundance, and excess becomes disaster; one yang below merely preserves a gasping breath; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Gasping, a thread of breath” means sinking toward oblivion. “Bowing low and prostrate” means at the end, with none to appeal to. In this hexagram one yang is veiled beneath doubled yin — the image of the utmost distress. Divining about illness means certain death. In battle there is sure defeat. The imprisoned are hard to release. The litigant does not prevail. In all affairs there is misfortune.
shi: Keeping to the old ways will yet turn out well; pressing into contention will surely reach punishment. Calm your heart and hold on in waiting — do not envy another’s glory.

name: Hexagram of Growing Yin
note: Pure yin with no response; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: Doubled yin above, the ghostly vapor floats and overflows; the inner courtyard is deep in water, and boats are rowed beneath the hall.
yan: A hexagram of pure yin, with within and without not answering each other; disasters of officials and ghosts alike belong to yin. In all affairs it is so — the image of misfortune and decline. Yet though within and without do not answer, if the power of officials helps, then it turns again to good fortune.
he: The traveler meets robbers; in all affairs it is unfavorable. Of secret plots and disputes one must be most careful. Another edition says: a hexagram of enlightenment, all affairs mildly auspicious. With water flowing before the hall and boats rowed beneath it, it is fitting only to pray for rain. Zhang Nanxuan divined about rain and the answer indeed came true.
chen: The three positions are all yin, and two grows again; the yang force must be cut off, and one stops midway, unable to act; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Doubled yin above” means the way of yang is blocked. “The courtyard deep in water” means the anxiety of drowning. In this hexagram pure yin has no response — the image of disaster. The diviner who obtains it will be harmed by women of the yin sort and by robbers. For the sick it is greatly inauspicious. It also presages secret plots and curses, official ghosts, and disputes; in all affairs it is inauspicious, and only praying for rain is fitting.
shi: Against petty men of yin you must guard with care; gate and courtyard are not yet at peace. Within the house there is much clamor and noise — disputes arise in the dark.

name: Hexagram of Withdrawal from the World
note: Yang’s light out of place; Zhen, thunder of the due east.
xiang: Beset by disaster and misfortune, he shuts the door and sits alone; his followers are scattered and gone, and there is no way to fetch a fire.
yan: The yang force is out of place and has no following, and so it is called sitting alone. Fire is of the yang kind, the resource of cooking; a host of yin cuts it off, and there is no way to fetch it. The dwelling meets with disaster and ruin, and in all affairs one cannot be satisfied. In marriage there is no offspring. The traveler has not returned. The sick do not recover. This hexagram is greatly inauspicious; one must be most careful.
he: The sick do not recover. Official affairs are not resolved. The family’s way keeps to the old; be wary of secret plots. Trade brings no profit. A military expedition loses discipline.
chen: Three yang below is the image of the worthy man in the wilds. A host of yin above means the way of petty men grows; one should not show oneself.
liu: “Beset by disaster” means yin rides over yang. “No way to fetch a fire” means the dim cannot be made bright. In this hexagram yang is out of place and without followers, while yin ascends and its faction flourishes. The diviner who obtains it will meet with unlooked-for disaster — a greatly inauspicious hexagram.
shi: The fortune is harsh and truly to be grieved; sorrow and grief through spring and autumn. For now, plan to flee to the northwest — do not toil or seek beyond yourself.

name: Hexagram of Every Misfortune
note: Pure yin seen together; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: Disaster and misfortune descend with violence; in all affairs it is unfavorable; illness and entanglement with officials — at every move one stumbles and falls.
yan: The three positions are all yin, with the dark stars descending together; disaster and misfortune must come. Whether going out or staying, speaking or keeping silent, in nothing is there good fortune.
he: In this hexagram all disasters break out at once; for the sick it is all the more inauspicious; what is sought does not succeed; in all affairs it is unfavorable.
chen: Twelve is the extreme number of Heaven and earth. Now that yin has reached its extreme, the will to life is cut off and cannot return. This hexagram is the last of the one hundred and twenty-four hexagrams, the place where all transformations come to rest; its inauspiciousness can be known.
liu: “Utmost yin without yang” means the extreme of exhaustion. “At every move one stumbles” means there is no way to use one’s strength. In this hexagram the three positions are all exhausted yin, and every misfortune breaks out at once; whatever is done is obstructed — one can only await the end.
shi: At the tip of a hundred-foot pole the road has ended; thinking it over, no plan, he turns to drift like the windblown tumbleweed. Intent only on landing the white perch on his line, unaware, he topples over into the waves.
